transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you, and thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um... well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but... what brings me in is that I've been feeling, well, like I'm constantly running on a motor lately. I mean, I teach special education, so being on the go is usually a good thing, right? But it’s gotten to where I finish one thing at school, or even at home, and I just immediately jump into the next project without ever really being able to... shut myself off. 

I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I do get a lot done, and I really try to be productive! But it's just getting a bit exhausting not being able to pause. Does that make sense? I hope that's the sort of thing you handle here.
How has your sleep been lately?

Oh, my sleep? Um... I think it's been pretty okay, actually. I mean, I usually just kind of collapse into bed at the end of the day because I've been going so hard, you know? But I try really hard to get a decent amount of rest so I can be at my best for my students the next morning. 

I don't think I have any real trouble sleeping, or at least nothing that really stands out to me as a problem. I hope that's okay? Is that... does that answer what you were asking?
During this period, have you had times when you felt unusually euphoric, overly upbeat, or almost abnormally high?

Oh, goodness, no. Um... no, I definitely wouldn't say that. I mean, I always try to keep a positive attitude, especially for my students, because they really need a cheerful environment. But I've never felt unusually euphoric or... or high, or anything like that. 

It's really just this physical feeling of needing to keep moving and doing things, rather than my mood being up in the clouds. I really hope I'm not making it sound like I'm totally out of control! I just like being helpful and getting things done, and lately my motor just won't switch off. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions the right way.
Have you had any period when you felt unusually irritable or easily angered?

Oh, gosh, no. Um... no, I really don't think so. I mean, in my line of work, you really have to have a lot of patience, you know? I pride myself on being very gentle and understanding with my kids. I don't really get angry easily at all. 

Even with this... this constant need to be doing something, I'm not mad or snappy with anyone. I just feel like I have to keep going. I try very hard to be pleasant to be around, so I really hope I haven't come across as irritable! Is that... I hope that answers what you were looking for?
Have you been needing much less sleep than usual and still felt completely energized?

Oh, um... no, not at all. I mean, like I said before, I usually just crash at the end of the day because I've been running around so much. I definitely still need my sleep! 

I really try to make sure I get enough rest so I can be patient and present for my students. I don't think I've ever had a time where I felt totally energized on just a little bit of sleep. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is that what you were asking?
Have you had problems with focus or attention since you were a child?

Oh, well... yes, I suppose I have. I mean, I always tried to mean well! My mother used to joke that even back in elementary school, I... I kind of taught the class from my seat. I was just very eager, you know? Always popping out of my chair, or talking, or... maybe sometimes cutting in before the teacher had quite finished giving directions. I just got so excited to participate and help out. 

So, yes, it's definitely been a part of who I was long before adulthood. It's not something that just started recently with this family change. It's... it's just how I've always been wired. 

I really hope I wasn't too much of a nuisance to my teachers back then! I always wanted to be a good student, just like I try so hard to be a good teacher for my own kids now. Is... is that the kind of background you were looking for? I hope I'm giving you helpful answers.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about different things most days?

Oh, goodness, no. Um... I really don't think so. I mean, obviously, I care very much about my students and want to do a good job, but I wouldn't say I'm a worrier. I always try to look on the bright side of things! 

I think it's just so important to stay positive, especially for the kids, you know? They really pick up on your energy. So I try very hard not to let myself get bogged down in worrying about things I can't control. I just keep moving forward and try to be as helpful and upbeat as I can be. 

Does... does that make sense? I hope that's a good thing, not being too much of a worrier. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I am!
Before age 12, did you often have trouble paying attention in school?

Oh, paying attention? Um... no, I really don't think that was the problem for me. I actually felt like I was paying attention to almost... well, everything! 

Like I was mentioning before with being so eager, I usually knew exactly what the teacher was saying. I just... I had a hard time waiting my turn to show it. But I definitely wasn't daydreaming or ignoring the lessons, I promise! I always wanted to be respectful and absorb what they were teaching. 

I hope I'm explaining the difference clearly enough? I just wouldn't want you to think I was ignoring my teachers. I really try to be as accurate as I can for you.
